input.content:
# word_count fix

## Root cause

`word_count` used `text.split(" ")`. When you pass an explicit separator, Python keeps the empty strings between adjacent separators and at the ends of the string. So `"".split(" ")` returns `['']` (count 1), and `"a  b".split(" ")` returns `['a', '', 'b']` (count 3). Tabs and newlines also weren't treated as word separators.

## Fix

Switched to `text.split()` with no arguments. It splits on any run of whitespace and drops leading and trailing whitespace, so it never produces empty strings. Also added type hints (`text: str -> int`), as the project conventions require.

## Test

Added two regression tests in `tests/test_textutils.py`:

- `test_regression_word_count_empty`: `""` gives 0 and `"   "` gives 0
- `test_regression_word_count_repeated_spaces`: `"a  b"` gives 2, `"  a b  "` gives 2, and `"a\tb\nc"` gives 3

Both failed before the fix (1 != 0, 3 != 2) and pass after it. The full suite passes with `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .`.
